name: Chris Mensalvos
bio: Chris Mensalvos was a Filipino leader of ILWU Local 37, the Seattle Filipino cannery workers' union, targeted for deportation under the McCarran (Internal Security) Act for his union and alleged Communist activity. His case was part of the McCarthy-era drive to deport foreign-born trade unionists for their labor and political activity.
charges: Deportation proceedings under the McCarran (Internal Security) Act for alleged Communist affiliation and radical union activity.

bio: Anna Ganley was a Detroit radical, active in Scottsboro defense and anti-war work, who faced deportation on the testimony of paid informer witnesses during the McCarthy era. name: Norman Tallentire
bio: Norman Tallentire was a foreign-born labor figure denied U.S. citizenship because of his militant labor background during the McCarthy era. His case was among those featured in the National Guardian's 1952 reporting on the drive against foreign-born radicals and trade unionists.
charges: Denied U.S. citizenship under the McCarran (Internal Security) Act for alleged Communist affiliation and militant labor activity.
convicted: Faced denial of citizenship (no criminal conviction).

name: Antonia Sentner
bio: Antonia Sentner of St. Louis was harassed with deportation proceedings as a hostage for her husband, UE organizer William Sentner, during the McCarthy era. Her case was among those featured in the National Guardian's 1952 reporting on the drive to deport foreign-born radicals and trade unionists.
charges: Deportation proceedings under the McCarran (Internal Security) Act for alleged Communist affiliation and radical union activity.

name: Charles Tuteur
bio: Charles Tuteur was a German emigre who faced denaturalization during the McCarthy era for having read three publications the government deemed subversive. His case was among those featured in the National Guardian's 1952 reporting on the drive against foreign-born radicals.
charges: Denaturalization proceedings under the McCarran (Internal Security) Act based on reading publications deemed subversive.

name: Mugo Gatheru
bio: Mugo Gatheru was a Kenyan student at Lincoln University, Pennsylvania, ordered deported under the Internal Security Act on an alleged passport-fraud basis and targeted as a 'subversive' anti-colonial African. His case was among those featured in the National Guardian's 1952 reporting on McCarthy-era deportations.
charges: Deportation proceedings under the McCarran (Internal Security) Act based on alleged passport fraud, targeting anti-colonial activity.

name: Charles Chaplin
bio: Charlie Chaplin, the film star, was barred from re-entering the United States under the McCarran Act while abroad at sea, pending a 'subversive'-activities inquiry into his left-wing political associations. His case was among those featured in the National Guardian's 1952 reporting on McCarthy-era political exclusions.
charges: Barred from U.S. re-entry under the McCarran Act pending a 'subversive activities' inquiry into his political views.
convicted: No — an exclusion/re-entry bar, not a criminal case.
sentence: Effectively exiled from the United States.
